segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Ukraine pause, Israel votes, Brazil reels
bullets: Local Russia-Ukraine pause begins near Oleshky
Israeli election voting is underway
Brazil markets plunge after Lula's win
Anthropic files for a public offering

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Tuesday, October twenty-seventh.
A local pause begins near Ukraine's Oleshky, while Kyiv reports damage from a fresh attack. Israel votes in a national election, with no result yet.
Brazil's market takes a historic-sized hit after Lula's win. Anthropic files to go public, and a sunken drilling rig off Gabon still has five people unaccounted for.

segments.strap: LOCAL PAUSE IN OLESHKY; KYIV REPORTS NEW DAMAGE
segments.headline: A local pause, with fighting elsewhere

graphic.title: Oleshky pause begins as Kyiv is hit
bullets: Russia and Ukraine say local pause began
Aid and civilian evacuation cited as purpose
AFP could not verify less fighting
Kyiv reports bridge and metro damage

lines.text: Russia and Ukraine say a localized pause around Oleshky began early Tuesday to allow humanitarian work and civilian evacuation. Russia's Defense Ministry says fire toward Kherson stopped. Ukraine's human rights ombudsman says Ukraine is honoring the arrangement.
This is a small, local pause, not a general ceasefire. A.F.P. could not verify that fighting had decreased, and the sides gave no end time.
On the same morning, Kyiv reported ballistic warnings and damage to the Southern Bridge and metro infrastructure. The pause in one area did not stop attacks elsewhere.

segments.strap: U.S. IRAN STRIKE PLANS REPORTED; TEHRAN TALKS CONTINUE
segments.headline: U.S. military options and Iran diplomacy

graphic.title: Plans reported; no strike reported
bullets: CNN cites two U.S. officials on possible operations
Officials say action could follow midterms
Trump said there would be no strike Monday
Iran says indirect talks continue

lines.text: C.N.N., citing two U.S. officials, reports that American forces in the region could begin new, potentially major operations within ninety-six hours of an order from President Trump. The officials said plans are ready and action could come after the midterm elections. This is reporting about a possible order, not an order.

President Trump said there would be no strike Monday. Iran says indirect talks are continuing, and officials from Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met in Tehran and agreed to keep talking. No settlement was announced.

Separately, the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed missile sites in Yemen and intercepted three Houthi missiles and four drones headed toward Saudi Arabia. That is the coalition's account; the captured report did not give a full damage or casualty count.

segments.strap: ISRAEL VOTES; NETANYAHU WARNS OF IRANIAN ATTACK
segments.headline: Israel votes as regional tensions remain high

graphic.title: Polls open, no result yet
bullets: Voting for the 120-seat Knesset
Results not available at capture cutoff
Netanyahu warns of possible Iran-linked attack
No attack reported in the capture

sources.name: The Jerusalem Post, polling stations open

lines.text: Voting has opened in Israel's election for the one-hundred-twenty-seat Knesset. Thirty-seven parties and lists are competing. The captured reports have no result or exit poll yet.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran or its proxies could attack before the vote and said Israel would respond. The Associated Press reported no attack in its account.

And a diplomatic meeting in Tehran brought officials from Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey together for security talks. They agreed to continue talking; no settlement or next meeting date was announced.

segments.strap: SERBIA'S STUDENT LIST LEADS IN PRELIMINARY COUNT
segments.headline: Serbia's partial count puts student list ahead

graphic.title: Preliminary count, not a final allocation
bullets: Results from 8,187 of 8,392 stations
Preliminary estimate: 140 seats to 104
Final count still pending

lines.text: Serbia's electoral commission has preliminary results from eight thousand one hundred eighty-seven of eight thousand three hundred ninety-two polling stations. The student-led list has fifty-two point seven one percent; President Aleksandar Vučić's list has thirty-nine point one seven.
The preliminary seat estimate is one hundred forty for the student list and one hundred four for Vučić's list. The count is not final, and those seats are not a final allocation.

segments.strap: BRAZIL STOCKS FALL 13.88% AFTER LULA'S ELECTION WIN
segments.headline: Brazil's first market day after the vote

graphic.title: Circuit breaker, steep selloff
bullets: First B3 circuit breaker since March 2020
Trading paused for 30 minutes
Treasury cancelled auctions for Oct. 27–29

lines.text: Brazil's Ibovespa fell thirteen point eight eight percent on Monday, closing at one hundred seventy-six thousand six hundred eight. The exchange halted trading for thirty minutes at the open, its first circuit breaker since March twenty twenty.
The Brazilian real fell more than eight percent. The Treasury cancelled debt auctions planned for Tuesday through Thursday and intervened twice, according to the captured reporting.
This was the first cash-market session after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election win. His opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, said he intended to seek annulment, but Reuters reported no court filing yet.

segments.strap: ANTHROPIC FILES FOR IPO; PROPOSED SYMBOL ANT
segments.headline: Anthropic files to go public

graphic.title: S-1 filed, offering not yet effective
bullets: SEC accepted Form S-1 on Oct. 26
Nasdaq Global Select Market planned
Price range and share count undetermined
Filing remains subject to SEC process

lines.text: Anthropic filed a public registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering. The company says it plans to list on Nasdaq under the symbol A.N.T.
The company says the number of shares and the price range have not been set, and the filing is not yet effective. This is paperwork toward an offering, not a completed stock listing.

The Associated Press and N.P.R. report first-half revenue of sixteen point three billion dollars, against a net loss of about eighty-one billion, mostly accounting charges according to the company. The prospectus filing is the event; the offering still has steps to go.

segments.strap: FIVE STILL MISSING AFTER GABON DRILLING RIG SINKS
segments.headline: Five people remain unaccounted for off Gabon

graphic.title: Prospector 5 sank offshore
bullets: Rig sank during preload on Oct. 24
One death reported by Reuters sources
Government had not confirmed a fatality

lines.text: A drilling rig sank off Gabon on Saturday. Its operator, Borr Drilling, says one hundred ten of the one hundred fifteen people aboard are safe. Five remain unaccounted for.
Reuters, citing sources, reported one death. Gabon's government had not confirmed that report in the captured account. The rig sank during a preload operation before drilling.

segments.strap: 47 REPORTED MISSING AFTER NAIROBI BUILDING COLLAPSE
segments.headline: Search continues after Eastleigh collapse

graphic.title: Day four of rescue operation
bullets: Kenya Red Cross figures
Prosecutors say inquiry file was not forwarded

lines.text: In Nairobi's Eastleigh district, the Kenya Red Cross says forty-seven people are reported missing after a building collapse. Two people have been rescued from the debris as the search enters its fourth day.
Kenya's prosecution service says the county never forwarded an inquiry file. The rescue count and that accountability question are both still moving.

segments.strap: NEW MEXICO FLOODWATERS RECEDE; RECOVERY HAZARDS REMAIN
segments.headline: Four Corners begins a difficult recovery

graphic.title: Flooding leaves closures and hazards
bullets: San Juan River levels falling
Hundreds of homes affected, report says
Shiprock bridge and road closures remain
Power out south of the river

sources.name: Yahoo News, road and power update

lines.text: Floodwaters are receding across northwestern New Mexico, but the Four Corners region is far from back to normal. Evacuated neighborhoods remain closed, and hundreds of homes were affected, according to AccuWeather.
K.S.U.T. reports the San Juan River at Farmington rose to thirteen times its usual size, breaking a record set in nineteen oh nine. Sewage and chemical contamination are among the recovery hazards.
The bridge on U.S. sixty-four at Shiprock remains closed, another stretch of U.S. sixty-four is shut, and power is still out south of the river. No deaths had been reported through Monday.

segments.strap: INDIA MOVES THOUSANDS AHEAD OF CYCLONE ARNAB
segments.headline: Cyclone preparations spread across eastern India

graphic.title: Evacuations and transport plans
bullets: Odisha and Andhra Pradesh prepare
Fishing boats return to harbour
Rail cancellations listed for Oct. 27 and 28

lines.text: Authorities in eastern India are preparing for Cyclone Arnab. In Odisha's Gajapati district, two hundred ten pregnant women have been moved to maternity or health facilities. Andhra Pradesh plans to move more than four thousand seven hundred.

Officials have identified fifteen thousand vulnerable people and two hundred eighty-one shelters in Gajapati. More than thirty thousand fishing boats have returned to Andhra harbours, and rail services listed dozens of cancellations.

segments.strap: KENYA RELEASES 20 EBOLA CONTACTS; 98 REMAIN QUARANTINED
segments.headline: Kenya eases Ebola quarantine for some contacts

graphic.title: Twenty contacts complete quarantine
bullets: Released after 21 symptom-free days
Further releases expected in November

lines.text: Kenya released twenty Ebola contacts from quarantine after they completed twenty-one days without symptoms. Ninety-eight contacts remain quarantined, according to the captured reporting.
Kenya had reported nine cases and two deaths. Those releases are a step in monitoring; they do not mean the outbreak is over.

segments.strap: UK SANCTIONS 15 SUDANESE COMMANDERS OVER ATROCITY CLAIMS
segments.headline: UK targets commanders from Sudan's warring forces

graphic.title: Travel bans and asset freezes
bullets: Fifteen RSF and SAF commanders sanctioned
UK cites suspected atrocities and sexual violence
One year since El Fasher fell

sources.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

lines.text: The United Kingdom has sanctioned fifteen commanders from Sudan's Rapid Support Forces and Sudanese Armed Forces, imposing travel bans and asset freezes.
The U.K. government says the sanctions respond to suspected atrocities, including sexual violence, a year after the fall of El Fasher.

segments.strap: MICROSOFT OFFERS VOLUNTARY EXITS TO ABOUT 60,000 STAFF
segments.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages

graphic.title: Exit offer reaches about 27% of workforce
bullets: United States, Canada, India and UK
Company cites changing work and AI investment

lines.text: The Associated Press reports Microsoft offered voluntary exit packages to about sixty thousand employees, around twenty-seven percent of its global workforce.
The offer spans the United States, Canada, India and the United Kingdom. Microsoft says its work is changing and it is investing in artificial intelligence.

segments.strap: JAPANESE CLOUD CYBERATTACK MAY AFFECT 26,739 SERVERS
segments.headline: Japanese provider reports a large cloud attack

graphic.title: GMO Internet describes possible server impact
bullets: Company says attack hit cloud service
CEO says ransom demand was $50 million

lines.text: GMO Internet says a cyberattack on its cloud service may have affected twenty-six thousand seven hundred thirty-nine servers. The company linked the incident to unauthorized trading at more than seventy firms.

Euronews reports the company's chief executive said the attackers demanded fifty million dollars in cryptocurrency. Those figures are company and press claims; the impact count is described as potential.

segments.strap: MILWAUKEE LEADS SERIES 3–0; DALLAS BEATS PHILADELPHIA
segments.headline: A lopsided night in baseball and football

graphic.title: Brewers one win from the title
bullets: Milwaukee beats Tampa Bay 10–1 in Game 3
Brewers lead World Series 3–0
Dallas defeats Philadelphia 38–21
NBA signs multi-year Polymarket and Kalshi deals

lines.text: In the World Series, Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay ten to one in Game Three and now leads three games to none. The Associated Press says Brandon Woodruff returned after a shoulder injury.
Dallas beat Philadelphia thirty-eight to twenty-one on Monday night. The Cowboys turned a Monday into a good one; the Eagles are having the opposite sort of week.
The N.B.A. also signed multi-year deals with prediction-market operators Polymarket and Kalshi. The terms were not disclosed.

segments.strap: NASA AND USDA EXPAND EARTH DATA FOR FARMING
segments.headline: NASA and USDA widen agriculture data work

graphic.title: Earth observations for crops and disasters
bullets: New memorandum between NASA and USDA
Crop estimates and drought assessment
Support disaster assessment with geospatial data

lines.text: NASA and the U.S. Department of Agriculture signed an agreement to expand the use of Earth observation and mapping data in agriculture.
The agencies say the work will support crop estimates, drought monitoring and disaster assessment. They signed the agreement on October twenty-fourth; NASA announced it Monday.

The Verge, Apple acknowledges display issue

lines.text: The Associated Press says Federal Reserve policymakers are likely to leave the key interest rate unchanged Wednesday. That is a preview, not the decision.
Brent crude settled at about one hundred sixteen dollars a barrel Monday after topping one hundred seventeen intraday, according to C.N.B.C.
From the M.S.I. headline capture: The Verge reports Instagram Reels can now be watched on Apple TV, and says Apple acknowledged an iPhone Duo display issue after reports of cracked screens.

The Jerusalem Post reports the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations office logged a vessel on fire off Iraq's coast. The capture did not identify the vessel, cause or casualties. And Reuters reports France's interior minister counted one thousand four hundred thirty-five arrests and two hundred sixty-seven officers injured in Monday's protest unrest.
